primitives.note: Q's charge-up (up to ~3-4s, self-slowing) blocks other actions until recast fires the beam; R's channel (up to 10s) blocks other actions while enabling up to 4-6 Arcane Barrage recasts.
Q is an active/recast pair (charge then beam); R is a channel with multiple separately-timed Arcane Barrage recasts, each its own damage instance.

Arcane Perfection: landing an Arcane Barrage on an enemy champion (the dummy counts as one) grants a stack (cap 3-5 by rank) that increases the damage of subsequent Arcane Barrage casts, but not the cast that granted the stack.

Mana costs (Q/W 80-120, E 60-80, R flat 100) meaningfully gate how many casts fit in a 15s fight; Mana Surge (P) restores mana on the next empowered basic attack, doubled vs champions, partially offsetting spend.
Single damage instance dealt after a short cast time / travel-or-impact delay, then on cooldown.
Eye of Destruction deals 66.7% increased damage (x1.667) if the target is in the inner 'epicenter' radius versus the outer effect radius; the dummy fight must assume which the target occupies.

needsBespoke.why: Every damage-relevant mechanic (Q's charge/recast, W's plain cast with an epicenter damage multiplier, E's plain cast, R's channel/multi-recast with a per-stack self-buff, and mana as a binding resource) decomposes into existing primitives; nothing requires bespoke logic beyond them.

proposal: Enter the fight at full mana.
Cast Q (Arcanopulse): begin the charge and recast at minimum charge time to fire the beam as fast as possible for early damage and to start its cooldown (cdstart is post-effect).
Cast E (Shocking Orb) for its flat magic damage.
Cast W (Eye of Destruction) on the dummy, aiming for the epicenter for maximum damage.

Cast R (Rite of the Arcane): channel and recast Arcane Barrage as fast as the 0.6s per-shot interval allows, using all available recasts (4-6 by rank); each recast after the first benefits from Arcane Perfection stacks built by hitting the dummy on prior casts.
After R ends (or its recasts are exhausted), resume weaving Q, W, and E on cooldown in whatever order they come off cooldown, mana permitting.
Auto-attack in any gap where no ability is off cooldown or affordable, both for the small extra damage and to trigger Mana Surge's mana restoration.
Repeat until the 15s fight window ends.
questions: Should R be opened immediately for its long cooldown and stacking payoff, or held until after Q/W/E have been used once so mana is spent optimally?
Against a single stationary dummy, does Arcane Perfection reliably reach its stack cap (3-5) before R's recasts are exhausted, or should the rotation assume partial stacking only?
Is auto-attacking between casts actually worth it given Xerath's low base AD and lack of any on-hit damage rider, or should mana always be held for the next spell cast instead?
Does the simulator enforce a fixed real-time duration for Q's charge and R's channel regardless of how fast the player recasts, or does recasting immediately shorten the time these abilities occupy?
